content.title: About
content.content: Cereal is a ready‑to‑eat breakfast made from whole or processed grains (wheat, oats, rice, corn, etc.) that are toasted, often sweetened, and formed into flakes. The product has a light, crunchy texture and a neutral flavor, making it a popular quick‑morning option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑made cereal was created in the late 19th century by John Harvey Kellogg in the United States.
There are more than 30 varieties, including whole‑grain, gluten‑free, and vitamin‑fortified options.
Cereal is frequently used as a base for granola bars, muesli, and dessert recipes.
In many countries it is served with milk, yogurt, fruit, or nuts.
Fortified cereals may contain added B‑vitamins, iron, and calcium.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cereal provides slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain satiety for several hours.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions contain fiber that supports healthy digestion and gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6 and folate aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Fortified with minerals
items.content: Many cereals are enriched with iron, calcium and magnesium to help address common deficiencies.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many processed breakfasts, plain cereal typically contains little fat unless nuts or oils are added.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweetened cereals can contain up to 30 % sugar, increasing the risk of cavities and weight gain.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Most wheat, barley or rye cereals contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some varieties include nuts, soy protein or dairy additives that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Additive concerns
items.content: Artificial flavors and preservatives can cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cereal is typically poured over milk, kefir, or a plant‑based drink and left for 1–2 minutes. It can be topped with fresh berries, banana slices, nuts, honey, or dried fruit to boost nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crunch.
